deed: פרופ׳ חוסאם חאיק המציא אף מלאכותי שמאבחן מחלות מנשיפת האוויר
title: Prof. Hossam Haick of the Technion developed an artificial nose that identifies 17 diseases from a single breath

trailer.text: Prof. Hossam Haick is an Arab-Israeli scientist and engineer and a Full Professor at the Technion, born in 1975 in Nazareth into an Arab Christian family.
At the Technion he developed an "artificial nose" that diagnoses diseases through chemical analysis of exhaled breath.
The array is called Na-Nose. It is based on gold particles and carbon tubes, and it diagnoses and classifies 17 diseases from a single breath.
According to Haick, in a study of 1,404 subjects in five countries, the system detected and sorted the diseases with an average accuracy of 86%.
In 2026, Haick received the Presidential Medal of Honour.

paragraphs.text: Hossam Haick was born in 1975 in Nazareth, into an Arab Christian family.
He is not a medical doctor.
He did his doctorate in the field of energy, and only later switched to biomedical technology.
After a postdoc at Caltech he returned to the Technion.
In 2006 he joined the faculty as an Assistant Professor in the Wolfson Faculty of Chemical Engineering.
That is also when he began developing the device.
Haick said his inspiration was dogs that identify disease.
The device is a white desktop box with a tube.
A person exhales into the tube, and the breath is sent into an array of sensors.
Some of the sensors are made of layers of gold nanoparticles, and others of a random network of carbon nanotubes.
When volatile compounds from the breath bind to the ligands, the electrical resistance between the nanoparticles or nanotubes changes.
The signal is sent to a computer.
Haick explained that instead of a nose there are chemical sensors, and instead of a brain there are algorithms, as with dogs that identify a smell.
As early as 2009, a paper of his in Nature Nanotechnology demonstrated the diagnosis of lung cancer from exhaled breath using sensor arrays with gold nanoparticles.
Between January 2011 and June 2014, samples were collected from 1,404 subjects.
They were recruited in the United States, Israel, France, Latvia and China.
First, using mass spectrometry, the group identified the compound signatures of 17 diseases.
The diseases included lung, bowel, head and neck, ovarian, bladder, prostate, kidney and stomach cancer, as well as Crohn's disease.

At an earlier stage, separately from the study on the 17 diseases, the team tested the device in clinics on more than 8,000 patients, to teach the software to distinguish between disease and confounding factors.
Gender, age, smoking and geographic location were found to have a negligible effect on the sample.
According to Haick, the system detected and sorted the diseases with an average accuracy of 86%.
Until this study, efforts of this kind were mainly used to detect a single disease.
According to ynet, the paper gave the first scientific proof of a 2,400-year-old hypothesis that breath tests may provide information about clinical conditions.
Haick said that every disease has a chemical signature that distinguishes it from other diseases and from a normal state of health.
In clinical studies the device distinguished between stages of stomach cancer and lung cancer, as early as stage one.
In four out of five cases, the NaNose chip distinguished between benign and malignant lung lesions, and even between cancer subtypes.
Haick said the aim is to detect disease at an early stage and raise the survival rate.
A joint study by Beilinson and the Technion examined whether atherosclerotic heart disease can be predicted with a breath test.
About 60 patients with no known heart disease, who came to the Beilinson emergency department because of chest pain, were tested.
The test separated normal arteries from atherosclerosis with a sensitivity of 69% and a specificity of 67%.
The common coronavirus tests were done by taking a sample from the mucous membranes of the nose and throat and by testing by a professional team in a laboratory.
Between taking the test and getting the result, several to many days passed.
According to the Technion, a non-invasive, rapid and inexpensive method was needed to screen carriers.
A team led by Prof. Haick and Dr. Yoav Broza of the Technion developed a breath device for coronavirus.
The device is similar in size to a smartphone, and there is no need to touch it, so there is no infection between subjects.
In a preliminary clinical study in Wuhan, China, it detected markers of the disease with 92% accuracy, 100% sensitivity and 84% specificity.
Haick said that the system succeeded in distinguishing between people with lung diseases and people with coronavirus.
The study was funded by the Technion and published in the journal ACS Nano.
The device's artificial intelligence can be adapted to any other infectious disease.

stations.title: From the lab to the phone

paragraphs.text: According to IEEE Spectrum, at the time the study was published Haick was working on miniaturizing the device, in the hope of adding it as a module to smartphones.
The project, SniffPhone, is funded by the European Commission with a grant of six million euros.
In 2018 SniffPhone won the European Commission Innovation Prize in Lisbon.
Nanose Medical holds an exclusive license for medical uses of the technology.
According to Haick, seven companies have licensed the research underlying the technology in order to create a commercial product.
Haick noted that the array can also be used to detect food spoilage.
According to Haick, the production cost of each breath device for detecting coronavirus is about 1,000 dollars, and in industrial production it can be brought down to a few hundred.
He said the system is inexpensive, non-invasive and portable, and therefore suitable for wide screening.
GOOD magazine included Haick among the 100 people changing the world for the better.
He was included in the list from 2015 to 2018.
The list includes people from 37 countries.
Haick also received the Humboldt Research Award in Germany.
In 2026, he received the Presidential Medal of Honour and became a Fellow of the United States National Academy of Inventors.
He has more than 500 scientific publications and more than 100 patents.
He is a co-founder of five companies that emerged from academic research.
Haick pioneered the first mass online course in Arabic on nanotechnology, and more than 5,000 students took it.
Dr. Mangilal Agarwal, who was not involved in the development, said that Haick's group is ahead of his group in terms of getting close to tests at the doctor's clinic.
Jonathan Beauchamp said the study demonstrates the power and promise of the technique.

stations.title: What has not yet been proven

paragraphs.text: According to Jonathan Beauchamp, it is accepted in the breath research community that compounds unique to specific diseases probably do not exist.
Dr. George Preti said it is hard to distinguish in breath samples between chemicals from the body and chemicals from the environment.
According to Haick himself, prostate, breast and bladder cancer are hard to diagnose from breath, and other tests may be more suitable.
The coronavirus test still needs a larger study to validate the results.
The heart data are only preliminary.
According to Haick, the system is in the process of commercialization and needs to go through regulatory processes.

disagreements.question: What was the accuracy in detecting stomach cancer?

versions.says: According to IEEE Spectrum, in a blinded test the device detected gastric cancer with 92 to 94 percent accuracy.
According to the Times of Israel, in a 2014 study in Gut the NaNose system was 80% as effective in detecting gastric cancer as the standard method for detecting the disease, GCMS.

disagreements.question: How many institutions took part in the 17-disease study?

versions.says: According to Smithsonian, researchers from 14 research institutions in five countries
According to ynet, 14 departments in 9 medical centers in 5 countries

disagreements.question: On how many diseases was the device trained?

versions.says: According to IEEE Spectrum, the lab trained it on more than 23 diseases
According to IEEE Spectrum, the study examined the discrimination among 17 diseases

claims.quote: מימוש הטכנולוגיה והמסחור שלה נערכים במסגרת חברת Nanose Medical. לחברה יש רישיון בלעדי להשתמש בטכנולוגיה של פרופ׳ חאיק מהטכניון

claims.text: לדברי חאיק, שבע חברות קיבלו רישיון למחקר שבבסיס הטכנולוגיה מהטכניון כדי ליצור מוצר מסחרי.
claims.quote: Seven companies have licensed the underlying research for the technology from Technion in hopes of creating a commercial product, Haick said.

claims.text: חאיק ציין שאפשר להשתמש במערך לבקרת איכות באמצעות זיהוי קלקול מזון.
claims.quote: the array could be used for quality control by detecting food spoilage

claims.text: לדברי חאיק, עלות הייצור של מכשיר היא כ-1,000 דולר, ובייצור תעשייתי אפשר להוריד אותה לכמה מאות.
claims.quote: עלות הייצור של כל מכשיר היא כ־1,000 דולר, אבל בייצור תעשייתי אפשר להוריד אותה לכמה מאות

claims.text: חאיק אמר שהמערכת זולה, לא פולשנית וניידת, ולכן אפשר להשתמש בה לסינון רחב למחלות.
claims.quote: He says that because it's affordable, non-invasive and portable, it could be used to screen widely for disease.

claims.text: לפי Times of Israel, מגזין GOOD כלל את חאיק בין 100 האנשים המשפיעים בעולם שמשנים אותו לטובה.
claims.quote: is one of the 100 most influential people in the world who are changing the world in a positive manner.

claims.text: חאיק נכלל ברשימת GOOD 100 משנת 2015 עד 2018.
claims.quote: was included in the GOOD 100 list of global citizens and creative change-makers from 2015 to 2018

claims.text: רשימת Good Magazine כוללת אנשים מ-37 מדינות התורמים לרווחת האנושות.
claims.quote: Good Magazine's 100 list includes people from 37 countries who contribute to the welfare of humankind in various aspects, including science, education, and business.

claims.text: חאיק קיבל גם את פרס המחקר של הומבולדט, שמוענק לחוקרים בולטים בשיתוף עם מוסדות מחקר בגרמניה.
claims.quote: Haick last weekend was also presented with the Humboldt Research Award, which recognizes top research done throughout the world in cooperation with research institutes in Germany.

claims.text: לחאיק יותר מ-500 פרסומים מדעיים ויותר מ-100 פטנטים, רבים מהם ברישיון לחברות בינלאומיות.
claims.quote: He has published more than 500 scientific publications and holds more than 100 patents, many of which have been licensed to international companies.

claims.text: חאיק הוא מייסד שותף של חמש חברות שצמחו ממחקר אקדמי.
claims.quote: Haick is a co-founder of five companies that emerged from academic research

claims.text: חאיק היה חלוץ הקורס המקוון ההמוני הראשון בערבית על ננוטכנולוגיה, עם למעלה מ-5,000 סטודנטים בעולם דובר הערבית.
claims.quote: Haick pioneered the first-ever mass online course in Arabic on nanotechnology, with over 5,000 students students in the Arabic-speaking world

claims.text: ד"ר מנגילל אגרוואל, שלא היה מעורב בפיתוח, אמר שקבוצתו של חאיק מקדימה את קבוצתו בדרך לבדיקות לביקור רופא.
claims.quote: Dr. Haick's group is certainly ahead of our group in terms of getting close to doctor's visit tests

claims.text: בושמפ אמר שהמחקר מדגים בבירור את העוצמה והתקווה שבטכניקת מערך חלקיקי הזהב.
claims.quote: The current study clearly demonstrates the power and promise of the gold nanoparticle array technique

claims.text: לפי ג'ונתן בושמפ, מקובל בקהילת חקר הנשיפה שתרכובות ייחודיות למחלות ספציפיות כנראה אינן קיימות.
claims.quote: it is now widely accepted within the breath research community that unique VOCs for specific diseases are unlikely to exist.

claims.text: ד"ר ג'ורג' פרטי אמר שקשה להבחין בין כימיקלים מהגוף לכימיקלים מהסביבה בדגימות נשיפה.
claims.quote: it's hard to distinguish body chemicals from environmental chemicals in breath samples because

claims.text: לדברי חאיק, קשה לאבחן סרטן הערמונית, השד ושלפוחית השתן לפי נשיפה, ולכן ייתכן שבדיקות אחרות מתאימות יותר.
claims.quote: It has been difficult to accurately diagnose prostate, breast, and bladder cancer based on exhalations, says Haick

claims.text: עדיין נדרש מחקר גדול יותר כדי לאמת את התוצאות.
claims.quote: While a larger cohort study is still needed to validate the results

claims.text: הנתונים בתחום הלב הם ראשוניים ומעודדים בלבד.
claims.quote: מדובר בנתונים ראשוניים מעודדים לגבי יכולת האבחנה והדיוק של המערכת

claims.text: לדברי חאיק, המערכת בתהליכי מסחור וצריכה לעבור תהליכים רגולטוריים.
claims.quote: המערכת נמצאת בתהליכי מסחור כי צריך לעבור תהליכים רגולטוריים. אנחנו עושים את המקסימום

claims.text: בשנה הקודמת מצא הצוות שהמכשיר זיהה סרטן קיבה במבחן סמוי בדיוק של 92 עד 94 אחוז.
claims.quote: the team found that the tool could detect gastric cancer in a blinded test of patients with 92- to 94-percent accuracy.

claims.text: במחקר מ-2014 שפורסם ב-Gut היתה מערכת NaNose יעילה ב-80% מהשיטה הסטנדרטית לגילוי סרטן קיבה.
claims.quote: In a 2014 study published in medical journal Gut, the NaNose system was 80% as effective in detecting the diseaase as the standard method of gastric cancer detection

claims.text: במחקר השתתפו עשרות חוקרים מ-14 מוסדות מחקר בחמש מדינות.
claims.quote: The study involved dozens of scholars based at 14 research institutions across five different countries.

claims.text: המעבדה אימנה את המכשיר על יותר מ-23 מחלות, ללמד אותו להבחין בין אדם בריא לאדם עם אחת המחלות.
claims.quote: The lab has trained the device on over 23 illnesses, teaching it to discriminate between a healthy individual and an individual with one of these catalogued diseases.

claims.text: המחקר הנוכחי השתמש לראשונה ב-Na-Nose לזיהוי והבחנה בין 17 מחלות בנשימה של 1,404 אנשים בחמש מדינות.
claims.quote: The current study, for the first time, used the Na-Nose to detect and discriminate among 17 different diseases in the breath of 1,404 individuals across five countries.

claims.text: חאיק אמר שבגלל בדיקות נוספות ורגולציה, המכשיר לא יהיה זמין בשוק או אצל רופאים במשך שנים רבות.
claims.quote: neither the Na-nose device nor any variations will be available on the market -- or in our doctor's offices -- for a number of years, said Haick.
